analysis.title: Americas Building - Homebuilders: A Heat Map for Housing: Decline in September Permits in Line with Weaker Demand as Mortgage Rates Hit 2 November 2026
key_insights: On a trailing 12-month basis, single-family permits contracted 5% in September, similar to last year and August. Builders are keeping inventory in line with weaker demand as mortgage rates reach the mid-7% range.
GS expects a low-to-mid single digit decline in new construction through year-end, given continued weakness in October.

GS says even a modest macro improvement could lower mortgage rates and give a better set up into early 2027 than currently expected. Two-year comps are easy, which points to upside for housing activity and builder results.
Near term, GS expects elevated incentives, company efforts to protect margins and a seasonal slowdown into year-end to weigh on investor sentiment.
Builders are adapting to the environment, including a shift to more build-to-order sales.

If conditions improve, GS sees the most upside in Buy-rated entry-level exposed names. MTH is cited for its broader product range and quick close strategy, and DHI for its geographic mix and capital allocation priorities.
Three-month single-family permits were flat in September vs +3% in August and -10% a year ago, and down 1% vs the comparable pre-pandemic period.
Among large new home markets, Virginia (+9%), Florida (+8%) and South Carolina (+7%) accelerated, offset by declines in Nevada (-23%), Arizona (-11%) and Utah (-5%).
25 states were flat to up on a three-month basis vs 33 in August. 7 states were up 5-10% and 9 grew 10%+, vs 13 and 11 in August.

Permits in the top 50 MSAs fell 2% YOY for the three months ended September vs +1% in August and -14% in September 2025. Daytona Beach, Columbus and Port St. Lucie posted the largest gains, while Colorado Springs, Las Vegas, New York and Philadelphia had the steepest declines.
On a two-year stack, Kansas City (+30%), Oklahoma City (+15%) and Tampa (+11%) led growth, while Las Vegas (-52%), Phoenix (-40%) and New York (-38%) lagged.

Zillow single-family home values were up 1% YOY in September, similar to August and vs flat last year, and are up 51% since September 2019. Realtor.com active listings rose 8% YOY for the week ended October 24.

In 2Q26 NAHB's Cost of Housing Index shows Indianapolis, Minneapolis, Atlanta and San Antonio as the most affordable large markets, needing 27-29% of median family income for a mortgage payment. Miami (58%), Riverside (48%), Las Vegas and Orlando (41% each) are the least affordable.

tension_points.bull_case: Easy two-year comps and a modest macro improvement could lower mortgage rates, giving a better set up into early 2027 and upside to housing activity and builder results, led by entry-level exposed names such as MTH and DHI.
tension_points.bear_case: Mortgage rates in the mid-7% range, continued weakness in October, elevated incentives, margin protection efforts and seasonal deceleration point to a low-to-mid single digit decline in new construction through year-end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A modest improvement in the macro that lowers mortgage rates would favor the bull case. Continued permit contraction through year-end would favor the bear case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Permits will decline into year-end on weak demand and high mortgage rates, but easy comps and any rate relief set up a better early 2027, with entry-level names MTH and DHI having the most upside.
theme_stances.evidence: we look for a low-to-mid single digit decline in new construction through year-end
